newsitem.title: CUBA: Mexico sends aid to Cuban hurricane victims.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sends aid to Cuban hurricane victims.

text.p: Mexico sent food and construction materials to Cuba on Wednesday to help victims of Hurricane Lili, which swept over the island last week, leaving thousands of people homeless and damaging crops.
Two Mexican Air Force planes flew in the 12 tonnes of food -- including rice, beans and oil -- and roofing tiles, arriving in Havana late on Wednesday.
Deputy Foreign Investment Minister Eliseo de Armas and Mexican Ambassador Claude Heller were at Havana airport to meet the shipment. Mexico has long been an ally of Cuba in the region.

Authorities have said that Hurricane Lili, which swept over western and central areas of Cuba last Thursday and Friday, destroyed more than 5,000 homes and damaged thousands more. The storm also caused widespread damage to crops, power lines and communications.
The aid from Mexico was the first to arrive in Cuba.
The Spanish government this week announced it was sending about $200,000 worth of emergency aid to the island.

Cuban-Americans, mostly in Florida, have mobilized to help victims. The U.S. government said on Wednesday it had waived a ban on direct flights to Cuba to allow a Roman Catholic charity to send a planeload of aid to Cuba.
The Cuban charity Caritas Cubana said on Wednesday that the flight, probably to the badly affected city of Cienfuegos, would arrive later this week with 78 tonnes of aid.
Caritas has appealed internationally for aid, and the Cuban government has also asked the U.N. development agencies to provide humanitarian assistance to help the island recover.
